questions.q: Which of the following will not act as an oxidising agent?
questions.explanation: Down group 6, the stability of the highest (+6) oxidation state increases (Cr < Mo < W), so MoO$_3$ is a much weaker oxidising agent compared to the Cr(VI) species.

questions.q: The highest oxidation state of manganese in fluoride is +4 (MnF$_4$), but the highest oxidation state in oxides is +7 (Mn$_2$O$_7$), because
options: Fluorine is more electronegative than oxygen
In covalent compounds, fluorine can form single bond only, while oxygen forms double bond
questions.explanation: Oxygen can form multiple (p$\pi$-d$\pi$) bonds with the metal, stabilising very high oxidation states, whereas fluorine (despite its higher electronegativity) can only form single bonds, so it cannot stabilise oxidation states as high as oxygen does.

questions.q: The calculated spin only magnetic moment of Cr$^{2+}$ ion is
questions.explanation: Cr$^{2+}$ has a 3d$^4$ configuration with 4 unpaired electrons, so $\mu = \sqrt{n(n+2)} = \sqrt{4\times 6} = \sqrt{24} \approx 4.90$ BM.

questions.q: In the following pairs, the one in which both transition metal ions are colourless is
questions.explanation: Sc$^{3+}$ (3d$^0$) and Zn$^{2+}$ (3d$^{10}$) have no unpaired d-electrons available for d-d transitions, so both are colourless.

questions.q: A member of the Lanthanoid series which is well known to exhibit +4 oxidation state is
questions.explanation: Cerium readily loses its single 4f electron in addition to the two 6s electrons to attain a stable [Xe]4f$^0$ configuration, giving a well-known +4 oxidation state.

questions.q: In which of the following pairs, both the elements do not have (n - 1)$d^{10}$ ns$^2$ configuration?
questions.explanation: Ag (4d$^{10}$5s$^1$) and Cu (3d$^{10}$4s$^1$) both have an ns$^1$, not ns$^2$, outer configuration, so neither has (n-1)d$^{10}$ns$^2$.

questions.q: The transition element ($\approx$5%) present with lanthanoid metal in Misch metal is
questions.explanation: Misch metal is about 95% lanthanoid metal and about 5% iron.

questions.q: Match the following: I. Zn$^{2+}$, II. Cu$^{2+}$, III. Ni$^{2+}$ with i. d$^8$ configuration, ii. Colourless, iii. $\mu$ = 1.73 BM. Codes:
questions.explanation: Zn$^{2+}$ (d$^{10}$) is colourless (ii); Cu$^{2+}$ (d$^9$) has one unpaired electron, $\mu$ = 1.73 BM (iii); Ni$^{2+}$ has a d$^8$ configuration (i).

questions.q: Which of the following statements related to lanthanoids is incorrect?
options: Lanthanoids are silvery white soft metals.
Ce$^{+4}$ solutions are widely used as oxidising agents in titrimetric analysis.
Colour of Lanthanoid ion in solution is due to d-d transition.
questions.explanation: The colour of lanthanoid ions arises from f-f transitions, not d-d transitions, making statement D incorrect.

questions.q: In which one of the following pairs, both the elements does not have (n-1)d$^{10}$ns$^2$ configuration in its elementary state ?
questions.explanation: Zn, Cd, Hg and Cn (Group 12) all have the (n-1)d$^{10}$ns$^2$ configuration, but Cu is [Ar]3d$^{10}$4s$^1$ and lacks this configuration, so the Cu, Zn pair is the one where it is not true that both elements have it.

questions.q: Which of the following is CORRECT with respect to melting point of a transition element ?
questions.explanation: Mn has an anomalously low melting point among the 3d transition metals because its half-filled 3d$^5$4s$^2$ configuration gives weaker metallic bonding, so Cr has a distinctly higher melting point than Mn.

questions.q: A transition metal exists in its highest oxidation state. It is expected to behave as
options: a central metal in a co-ordination compound
questions.explanation: In its highest oxidation state, a transition metal has a strong tendency to gain electrons and get reduced, so it behaves as an oxidizing agent (e.g., Mn in MnO$_4^-$).

questions.q: What will be the value of x in Fe$^{x+}$, if the magnetic moment $\mu$ = $\sqrt{24}$ BM ?
questions.explanation: $\sqrt{n(n+2)}$ = $\sqrt{24}$ gives n = 4 unpaired electrons, corresponding to a d$^6$ configuration, i.e. Fe$^{2+}$.

questions.q: (NH$_4$)$_2$Cr$_2$O$_7$ on heating liberates a gas. The same gas will be obtained by
questions.explanation: Ammonium dichromate decomposes on heating to give N$_2$ gas (along with Cr$_2$O$_3$ and H$_2$O). Heating NH$_4$NO$_2$ also gives N$_2$ + 2H$_2$O, the classic laboratory preparation of nitrogen gas.

questions.q: The only Lanthanoid which is radioactive
questions.explanation: Promethium (Pm) is the only lanthanide with no stable isotopes; all its isotopes are radioactive.

questions.q: All Cu(II) halides are known, except the iodide, the reason for it is that
options: Cu$^{+2}$ has much more negative hydration enthalpy.
questions.explanation: Cu$^{2+}$ is a strong enough oxidizing agent to oxidize I$^-$ to I$_2$, itself being reduced to Cu$^+$ (forming CuI), so Cu(II) iodide does not exist.

questions.q: Which of the following does not represent property stated against it?
options: Ti < V < Mn – Number of oxidation states
questions.explanation: Density actually increases across the 3d series from Sc to Fe (Sc lowest, Fe higher) due to increasing atomic mass with roughly similar atomic size, so 'Sc > Cr > Fe' is incorrect.

questions.q: Which one of the following is correct for all elements from Sc to Cu?
options: The lowest oxidation state shown by them is +2
4S orbital is completely filled in the ground state
3d orbital is not completely filled in the ground state
The ions in +2 oxidation states are paramagnetic
questions.explanation: From Sc$^{2+}$(d$^1$) to Cu$^{2+}$(d$^9$), every M$^{2+}$ ion in this series has at least one unpaired electron, so all are paramagnetic; the other statements have exceptions (e.g. Cr, Cu for 4s; Cu for 3d).

questions.q: Which of the following pairs has both the ions coloured in aqueous solution? [Atomic numbers of Sc = 21, Ti = 22, Ni = 28, Cu = 29, Mn = 25]
questions.explanation: Sc$^{3+}$(d$^0$), Ti$^{4+}$(d$^0$) and Cu$^+$(d$^{10}$) are colourless; Mn$^{2+}$(d$^5$) and Ti$^{3+}$(d$^1$) both have unpaired d-electrons and are coloured.

questions.q: Identify the set of paramagnetic ions among the following:
questions.explanation: Ti$^{3+}$(d$^1$), Cu$^{2+}$(d$^9$) and Mn$^{3+}$(d$^4$) all have unpaired electrons (paramagnetic); the other sets each contain a d$^0$ or d$^{10}$ (diamagnetic) ion (Sc$^{3+}$, Ti$^{4+}$, Zn$^{2+}$).

questions.q: How many moles of acidified K$_2$Cr$_2$O$_7$ is required to liberate 6 moles of I$_2$ from an aqueous solution of I$^-$?
questions.explanation: Cr$_2$O$_7^{2-}$ + 6I$^-$ + 14H$^+ \to$ 2Cr$^{3+}$ + 3I$_2$ + 7H$_2$O; 1 mol dichromate liberates 3 mol I$_2$, so 6 mol I$_2$ needs 2 mol K$_2$Cr$_2$O$_7$.

questions.q: Cu$_2$Cl$_2$ and CuCl$_2$ in aqueous medium
options: Cu$_2$Cl$_2$ is more stable than CuCl$_2$
CuCl$_2$ is more stable than Cu$_2$Cl$_2$
Stability of Cu$_2$Cl$_2$ is equal to stability of CuCl$_2$
questions.explanation: In water, the higher hydration enthalpy of Cu$^{2+}$ more than compensates for its higher ionisation energy compared to Cu$^+$, so Cu$^{2+}$ (CuCl$_2$) is more stable in aqueous medium; Cu$^+$ disproportionates.

questions.q: The elements in which electrons are progressively filled in 4f orbital are called
questions.explanation: Lanthanoids (atomic numbers 58-71) have electrons progressively filling the 4f orbitals.

questions.q: Incorrect statement with reference to Ce (Z = 58)
options: Atomic size of Ce is more than that of Lu.
Ce in +3 oxidation state is more stable than in +4.
Ce shows common oxidation states of +3 and +4.
questions.explanation: Ce4+ is actually a good oxidising agent (it readily gets reduced to the more stable Ce3+), so the statement that it is a reducing agent is incorrect.

questions.q: A mixture of NaCl and K$_2$Cr$_2$O$_7$ is heated with conc. H$_2$SO$_4$; deep red vapours are formed. Which of the following statement is false?
options: The vapours give a yellow solution with NaOH.
The vapours contain CrO$_2$Cl$_2$ and Cl$_2$.
The vapours when passed into lead acetate in acetic acid gives a yellow precipitate.
questions.explanation: The chromyl chloride test produces pure CrO2Cl2 vapours, not a mixture with free Cl2; statement B is therefore false, while A, C and D correctly describe the test.

questions.q: Which of the following statement is wrong?
options: In highest oxidation states, the transition metals show acidic character.
Metals in highest oxidation states are more stable in oxides than in fluorides.
Mn$^{3+}$ and Co$^{3+}$ are oxidizing agents in aqueous solution.
All elements of 3d series exhibit variable oxidation states.
questions.explanation: Not all 3d elements show variable oxidation states — e.g. Sc shows only +3 and Zn shows only +2 — so statement D is wrong.

questions.q: Oxidation state of copper is +1 in
questions.explanation: In cuprite (Cu2O), copper is in the +1 state; KEA also accepted chalcopyrite (CuFeS2), which is conventionally assigned Cu+1, Fe3+, S2-, giving copper a +1 state there too. Malachite and azurite are Cu(II) basic carbonates.

questions.q: Which of the following oxides shows electrical properties like metals ?
questions.explanation: CrO$_2$ shows metallic (in fact ferromagnetic, conducting) behaviour and is used in magnetic recording tapes, unlike the other insulating oxides listed.

questions.q: Which of the following is an amphoteric oxide ?
questions.explanation: Both V$_2$O$_5$ and Cr$_2$O$_3$ (intermediate oxidation state oxides of transition metals) react with both acids and bases, making them amphoteric.

questions.q: Which of the following oxidation states is common for all lanthanides ?
questions.explanation: All lanthanides show a common and most stable +3 oxidation state, though some also show +2 or +4 occasionally.

questions.q: The electronic configuration of transition element "X", is +3, oxidation state is [Ar]3d$^5$. What is its atomic number ?
questions.explanation: Adding back the 3 electrons lost to form the +3 ion ([Ar]3d$^5$) gives the neutral atom configuration [Ar]3d$^6$4s$^2$, i.e. atomic number 18+6+2 = 26 (Fe).

questions.q: KMnO$_4$ acts as an oxidising agent in alkaline medium. When alkaline KMnO$_4$ is treated with KI, iodide ion is oxidised to
questions.explanation: In alkaline/neutral medium, KMnO$_4$ oxidises iodide all the way to iodate, IO$_3^-$, being itself reduced to MnO$_2$.

questions.q: The magnetic nature of elements depends on the presence of unpaired electrons. Identify the configuration of transition elements which shows highest magnetic moment ?
questions.explanation: 3d$^5$ (e.g. Mn$^{2+}$) has the maximum possible number of unpaired electrons (5) among the given configurations, giving the highest magnetic moment.

questions.q: Which of the following statement is wrong regarding Lanthanoids ?
options: Ln(III) compounds are predominantly ionic in character.
The ionic size of Ln(III) ions decreases with increasing atomic number.
Ln(III) hydroxides are mainly basic in nature.
questions.explanation: Most Ln(III) ions have partially filled 4f orbitals and show colour due to f–f transitions, so 'generally colourless' is the wrong statement.

questions.q: The bivalent metal ion having maximum paramagnetic behaviour among the first transition series elements is,
questions.explanation: Mn$^{2+}$ (3d$^5$) has 5 unpaired electrons, the maximum among the given bivalent ions, giving it the highest paramagnetism.

questions.q: When a brown compound of Mn (A) is treated with HCl, it gives a gas (B). The gas (B) taken in excess reacts with NH$_3$ to give an explosive compound (C). The compounds A, B and C are;
options: A = MnO, B = Cl$_2$, C = NH$_4$Cl
questions.explanation: MnO$_2$ + conc. HCl gives Cl$_2$ gas; excess Cl$_2$ with NH$_3$ gives the explosive nitrogen trichloride, NCl$_3$.

questions.q: Mn$^{2+}$ compounds are more stable than Fe$^{2+}$ compounds towards oxidation to their +3 state, because
options: Mn$^{2+}$ is more stable with high 3rd Ionisation energy.
questions.explanation: Mn$^{2+}$ (3d$^5$, half-filled and extra stable) has a high third ionisation energy, so it resists oxidation to Mn$^{3+}$ more than Fe$^{2+}$ resists oxidation to Fe$^{3+}$.

questions.q: The electronic configuration of Gd$^{2+}$ is (at. no. of Gd is 64)
questions.explanation: Neutral Gd is [Xe]4f$^7$5d$^1$6s$^2$; removing 2 electrons for Gd$^{2+}$ removes the two 6s electrons first, giving [Xe]4f$^7$5d$^1$.

questions.q: On heating potassium permanganate, one of the following compound is not obtained:
questions.explanation: On heating, 2KMnO$_4$ decomposes to K$_2$MnO$_4$ + MnO$_2$ + O$_2$; MnO is not formed in this decomposition.

questions.q: Which one of these is not known?
questions.explanation: CuI$_2$ is not known/stable because I$^-$ (a strong reducing agent) reduces Cu$^{2+}$ to Cu$^+$, forming CuI + I$_2$ instead; CuBr$_2$, CuF$_2$ and CuCl$_2$ are all known, stable compounds.

questions.q: The correct statement is
options: Ce$^{+4}$ in aqueous solution is not known.
In general, lanthanoids and actinoids do not show variable oxidation states.
The extent of actinoid contraction is almost the same as lanthanoid contraction.
The earlier members of lanthanoid series resemble calcium in their chemical properties.
questions.explanation: The earlier lanthanoids (La, Ce etc.) are similar in size and chemical behaviour to Ca$^{2+}$/Ca-group elements due to comparable ionic radii, making statement (4) correct; Ce$^{4+}$ is a known stable oxidation state in aqueous solution, and actinoid contraction is greater per element than lanthanoid contraction.

questions.q: The electronic configuration of Cu$^{2+}$ ion is
questions.explanation: Cu atom is [Ar]3d$^{10}$4s$^1$; removing 2 electrons (4s first, then 3d) for Cu$^{2+}$ gives [Ar]3d$^9$4s$^0$.

questions.q: Which one of the following shows highest magnetic moment ?
questions.explanation: Fe$^{2+}$ (d$^6$, high spin) has 4 unpaired electrons giving the highest magnetic moment ($\approx$4.90 BM) compared to Co$^{2+}$ and Cr$^{3+}$ (3 unpaired) and Ni$^{2+}$ (2 unpaired).

questions.q: In a transition series, with the increase in atomic-number, the paramagnetism
options: first increases to a maximum and then decreases
first decreases to a minimum and then increases
questions.explanation: The number of unpaired electrons rises to a maximum around the middle of the series (e.g., d$^5$) and then falls, so paramagnetism first increases then decreases.

questions.q: The yellow precipitate formed during the chromyl chloride test is chemically .............
questions.explanation: $CrO_2Cl_2$ vapour is absorbed in $NaOH$ to give sodium chromate, which on treatment with acetic acid and lead acetate gives a yellow precipitate of lead chromate.

questions.q: The spin only magnetic moment of $Fe^{2+}$ ion (in BM) is approximately ...........
questions.explanation: High-spin $Fe^{2+}$ ($d^6$) has 4 unpaired electrons; $\mu=\sqrt{n(n+2)}=\sqrt{4\times6}=\sqrt{24}\approx5$ BM.

questions.q: In chromite ore, the oxidation number of iron and chromium are respectively ...............
questions.explanation: Chromite ore is FeCr$_2$O$_4$; balancing charges with O at -2 gives Fe as +2 and Cr as +3.

questions.q: The spin only magnetic moment of $Mn^{+4}$ ion is nearly ...................
questions.explanation: Mn$^{4+}$ has configuration 3d$^3$ (3 unpaired electrons); $\mu = \sqrt{3(3+2)} = \sqrt{15} \approx 3.87 \approx 4$ BM.

questions.q: The magnetic moment of a transition metal ion is $\sqrt{15}$ B.M. Therefore the number of unpaired electrons present in it is
questions.explanation: $\mu = \sqrt{n(n+2)}$; setting $n(n+2)=15$ gives n = 3 unpaired electrons.
